startup.name: Stilta
startup.description: Stilta sells agentic AI software to patent litigators, both law firms and in-house IP teams, who pay per seat or per matter to run source-backed, auditable analysis for challenging or enforcing patents. A Stockholm team of four engineers from consulting built it.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent with a 0.6 to 2 percent band (references/yc_acceptance.md). Up: four technical founders who have shipped AI systems at large organisations, a high-value paying buyer, and a wedge (auditability) that answers a real objection of lawyers. Down: no stated legal or IP background, no stated customers, and legal AI is crowded. The company is known to have been accepted, so this is for completeness only.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because the team is consultants without a lawyer or patent examiner on board, the pitch does not state paying customers or pilots, and legal AI already has well funded players such as Harvey and a patent specialist that raised a Series B in late 2025. A reviewer would ask why four engineers in Stockholm win trust with litigation partners in the United States.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B: seed cond 59% (n=126), series_a cond 26% (n=74), series_b cond 16% (n=19), series_c cond 0% (n=3, upper bound 16%); lower/known/upper seed 49/59/65, A 13/15/29.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Within 0.75 to 1.1 times the B2B anchor. Legal AI is the hottest vertical for seed money in 2026 and the team has enterprise AI delivery experience, offset by crowding and a European base selling to US litigators.

bands.rationale: Small pre seed or extension on top of the YC deal, common when a European team raises from regional funds.
Typical 2022+ B2B seed with median near 3.2M raise (base_rates run) and market seed deal size near 3M.
Upside from a hot legal AI category and consultant pedigree, using a lead from a US legal tech fund.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed stalls if the team cannot show a handful of paying litigation clients within the first year. Investors in legal AI have seen many demos, and analogs such as Abel (document review for litigation, shut down) and Cobbery (no round after YC) show that a pitch without a named law firm customer does not convert into a financing round.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B: seed cond 59% (n=126), series_a cond 26% (n=74), series_b cond 16% (n=19), series_c cond 0% (n=3, upper bound 16%); lower/known/upper seed 49/59/65, A 13/15/29.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Slightly above the 0.26 B2B anchor because litigation work has high contract values and the peer Solve Intelligence reached a Series A and B, but patent litigation is narrower than drafting.

bands.rationale: Thin round for a niche tool with a few dozen seats.
Median 2022+ Series A raise near 15M (cohort run) with market pre money near 60M.
Upside if Stilta becomes the standard litigation workflow at large IP firms.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails if usage stays in a few pilot matters and revenue does not pass roughly 1.5 to 2M annual recurring. Patent litigation is cyclical and concentrated in a few hundred firms, so growth can plateau. A broader player like Solve Intelligence, which expanded into litigation charting, can take the same buyers.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B: seed cond 59% (n=126), series_a cond 26% (n=74), series_b cond 16% (n=19), series_c cond 0% (n=3, upper bound 16%); lower/known/upper seed 49/59/65, A 13/15/29.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Above the thin 0.16 anchor by under 2x: legal software with sticky seats gets follow on rounds, and the one close analog (solve-intelligence) reached Series B within about 30 months.

bands.rationale: Flat or modest B for a niche vertical.
Series B median near 37M to 45M for 2022+ with post money often 300M or more.
Upside if expansion into trademark and prosecution wins.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B fails if the company is trapped as a litigation point tool whose growth is capped by case volume, while broader IP suites bundle comparable analysis. Investors want proof of expansion beyond the first workflow, and many niche legal AI products stop at a Series A, as Cognition IP and Edge show.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only (all cohorts): series_c cond 36% (n=55); B2B 2022+ has only n=3.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Below the all cohort 36 percent because patent litigation is a small market and a Series C needs a path to a very large market.

bands.rationale: Modest C. for this stage, scaled from the cohort round sizes and the current market medians.
Typical growth round. for this stage, scaled from the cohort round sizes and the current market medians.
Upside as an AI platform for all IP work.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C fails if the total market for IP software tops out below what a late stage investor needs, or if foundation model vendors and general legal assistants absorb the analysis. At that stage investors expect expansion beyond litigation, and few niche legal tools have shown it. Reaching it also needs the previous milestones on time, since investors at this stage compare the company with funded peers and late stage rounds in the analog set mostly went to firms with clear paying customers and fast revenue growth.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely end is an acquisition by a legal or IP software suite at modest value, or a stall at a small recurring revenue base. The market is narrow, competitors are well funded, and trust with litigators is slow to earn, so a large exit is unlikely but not impossible.

killers.risk: Narrow buyer base and cyclical case volume cap growth
killers.evidence: Patent litigation is concentrated in a few hundred firms and in-house teams, and peers such as Edge and Cognition IP show no or little follow on funding.
killers.mitigation: Expand to prosecution, invalidity and portfolio analysis early.

killers.risk: Better funded peers take the same customers
killers.evidence: Solve Intelligence raised a Series A in April 2025 and 40M Series B in December 2025 and added litigation features, and several other YC companies share the wedge.
killers.mitigation: Win a few anchor firms and own auditability and claim charting.

killers.risk: Trust and sales cycle with US litigators for a Swedish team
killers.evidence: Law firms buy through partners and security reviews, and the team has consulting not legal sales experience.
killers.mitigation: Hire a former patent litigator and sell through a design partner firm.

killers.risk: Foundation models and general legal assistants absorb the workflow
killers.evidence: Large legal AI vendors and model labs ship agent features that cover research, so a thin wrapper loses pricing power.
killers.mitigation: Deep proprietary data integrations and an audit trail that general tools lack.

competition_now.traction: Casetext bought by Thomson Reuters for 650M in 2023.

competition_now.what: Prior art search and patent analytics for R and D and IP teams.

competition_now.name: Manual review plus point solutions
competition_now.what: The status quo of associates and disconnected search tools.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agentic search over patents, prior art and litigation records with source citations is buildable by four strong engineers, but legal grade accuracy, evaluation and data licensing are hard, and quality must hold for high stakes claims. Small teams can ship a credible demo in three months but need years of evaluation work to earn trust.

takeover_risk.rationale: Well funded legal AI vendors already sell to the same buyers and could add litigation modules in under a year. The incentive is high because patent litigation fees are large, and distribution through existing law firm contracts favours them.

evidence.claim: Investors funded a patent AI peer with 12M and then 40M in 2025, signalling paid demand.
Thomson Reuters paid 650M for Casetext, showing legal AI is a real spend category.

roadmap.goal: Show legal credibility and a paying design partner before applying.
actions: Sign one or two IP litigation firms as design partners with written feedback.
Publish an accuracy benchmark on claim charting against associate work.
roadmap.proof: One named firm using it on live matters.

roadmap.goal: Convert pilots into paid seats and a lead round.
actions: Price per seat and per matter and close five paying firms.
Add a US based legal advisor and a US sales lead.
roadmap.proof: Five paying customers and 300K annual recurring revenue.

roadmap.goal: Prove repeatable sales beyond early adopters.
actions: Build SOC 2 and enterprise security reviews.
roadmap.proof: 1.5M to 2M annual recurring with 100 percent net retention.

roadmap.goal: Show a second product line and large customers.
actions: Land AmLaw 100 and large in-house teams.
Expand to trademark and other IP types.
Build integrations with docketing and portfolio systems.
Consider a European and Asian expansion.

pros.evidence: The pitch targets traceable outputs that litigators need for court.

brand.name: Stilta
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Stilta" --era 2022+ : invented name, 6 characters, 2 syllables; the invented kind in 2022+ has alive 92.7 percent, exit 4.4 percent (n=1826).
strengths: Distinct and likely available as a domain
weaknesses: Could be misspelled as Stilt or Stila
brand.rationale: An invented short name is the most common kind in 2022+ and shows no measurable effect on outcome. Legal buyers care about trust more than name, as with Harvey or Casetext, so brand is neutral here.

narrative.headline: A credible technical team in a funded legal AI category, but a narrow wedge against better funded peers makes a seed likely and a Series A a coin flip.
narrative.general_summary: Stilta sells to a small group of well paid buyers, patent litigators, in a category that investors clearly fund today. The cohort base rate for B2B seed within the YC set is near 59 percent and the legal AI wave pushes the first round to somewhat above that, while the Series A rate of 26 percent is held close to the anchor because the niche is narrow and Solve Intelligence already holds the best distribution. The most likely stop is after seed or Series A, with acquisition by an IP or legal suite as the most common good result.

assumptions: The description gives no customers or revenue, so none are assumed.
Funding data for 2022+ cohorts is incomplete and right censored, so conditional rates are lower bounds.
Seed means a round above 500K within 12 months of the batch start.
